setSeed

Source: R/utilities.R
setSeed.Rd

Set a global random seed for reproducible geodl workflows.

Usage

setSeed(seed)

Arguments

seed

Single integer random seed.

Value

Invisibly returns seed (as an integer).

Details

A geodl/torch training pipeline draws from two independent random number generator (RNG) streams: R's base RNG and torch's own RNG. setSeed() seeds both from a single value so that dataset shuffling, data augmentation, model weight initialization, and the training loop all produce identical results across runs.

The following sources of randomness are covered:

Dataset shuffling

torch::dataloader(..., shuffle = TRUE) and any dplyr::sample_n()-based shuffling (e.g. makeChipsDF(shuffle = TRUE)) read from R's base RNG.

Data augmentation

defineSegDataSet() and defineDynamicSegDataSet() choose which augmentations to apply and their magnitudes with base R functions (runif(), sample(), dplyr::sample_n()), which read from R's base RNG.

Model weight initialization

All defineXXX model constructors (e.g. defineUNet, defineDLab) rely on torch's default layer initializers, which draw from torch's RNG.

Training loop

Any stochastic operations inside luz::fit() (e.g. dropout, if present in a given architecture) draw from torch's RNG.

Call this before creating the dataset, dataloader, and model, and before calling luz::fit() — any random draws that occur before seeding will not be reproducible.

When torch::dataloader() is used with num_workers > 0, torch automatically reseeds each worker subprocess (with both set.seed() and torch::torch_manual_seed()) from the parent process's RNG state at the time the workers are spawned. As long as setSeed() is called once before the dataloader is created, and num_workers is held constant between runs, worker seeding is deterministic and requires no further action.

Full determinism on GPU is still subject to caveats outside this function's control: some cuDNN convolution algorithms are inherently non-deterministic regardless of RNG seeding, and torch's R bindings do not currently expose a "deterministic algorithms" toggle. For strict bit-for-bit reproducibility, training on CPU remains the most reliable option.
